subject: Order form: packaging, discount safeguards, and pass-through language (redlines)
messages:
From: Julia Shephard <julia.shephard@horizonhealth.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@horizonhealth.com
Date: Sun, 02 May 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Final order form and pricing questions

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement and Legal have reviewed the order form and have a few pricing/packaging items they want clarified before we proceed to signature:

- How will the seat-based "packaging seed" discount interact with the usage bands in Exhibit D if Horizon reduces seats during Year 2?
- Legal flagged the pass-through language for cloud egress and asked for a cap on any third-party passthroughs.
- They want clarity on the true-up model: retrospective quarterly true-up vs prospective monthly forecasting.

I've attached our annotated copy (Horizon_OrderForm_v3_redline.pdf). Can we get a short note on each of the bullets and a redline that addresses pass-through caps and the "fee collar" mechanics?

Julia
Director, Procurement
Horizon Health

Attachment: Horizon_OrderForm_v3_redline.pdf

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: Julia Shephard <julia.shephard@horizonhealth.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, priya_natarajan@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 02 May 2027 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Final order form and pricing questions

Hi Julia — thanks for the quick turn.

Appreciate the annotated copy. Quick answers up front:
- Packaging seed discount: the discount is applied to the seat component only and does not change the tier thresholds for usage bands in Exhibit D. If Horizon reduces seats in Year 2 we will apply a pro rata adjustment to the seat discount, but true-up on usage bands remains per the Exhibit (see proposed redline).
- Pass-through cap: we can accept a pass-through for third-party costs limited to actual third-party invoices + 5% admin fee, with a hard cap per quarter (proposal below).
- True-up: we prefer retrospective quarterly true-up for predictability, with an option for a prospective monthly forecast model if Horizon opts into the Forecasting Addendum.

I'll loop in Karthik and Laura to propose explicit redline language for Exhibit D and the Order Form. Can we target EOD Tuesday for a consolidated redline?

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Exec, Redwood Inference

Attachments: pricing-exhibit-draft_notes.txt

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, priya_natarajan@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 03 May 2027 09:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: Horizon redlines — Exhibit D (caps/floors), packaging, and discount smoothing

Team — compiling notes from Horizon's redline. Key asks and my risk callouts below. Please review and propose language edits inline.

Summary of Horizon asks:
- Cap on pass-throughs for cloud egress and managed services.
- Ability to reduce seat counts in Year 2 without penalty to usage band thresholds.
- Request for carry-forward credits for any unused committed units for up to 4 quarters.
- Ask to convert true-up to monthly prospective if our forecasting SLA is met.

Our concerns and proposed guardrails:
1) Pass-throughs: we can permit pass-throughs but must limit Redwood exposure. Propose: "Customer may pass through third-party charges reflecting actual invoices plus a 5% administrative fee; total pass-throughs recoverable by Redwood per calendar quarter shall not exceed USD 50,000 without Redwood prior written consent."

2) Seat reductions: agree pro rata on seat discounts, but usage band thresholds must be annualized. Proposed language: "Committed usage bands in Exhibit D shall be annualized for true-up purposes; temporary seat reductions within a 90-day window will not rebase the usage band thresholds unless a permanent amendment to the Order Form is executed."

3) Carry-forward credits: 4 quarters is high risk. Recommend limiting to 2 quarters and exclude onboarding credits.

4) Fee collar / smoothing: If we allow smoothing (i.e., aggregate by quarter to avoid spikes), require a one-time smoothing fee or a 3% reconciliation step on net overages.

Please add legal-gray phrasing and exact redline snippets. Priya — please review the pass-through cap numbers (50k) and suggest alternate ceilings if needed.

-Marissa

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, priya_natarajan@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 04 May 2027 08:50:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Internal: Horizon redlines — suggested sentence-level edits

Agree with Marissa. Two suggested edits for the Order Form redline:

1) Pass-through cap alternate: "Customer provided invoices for third-party fees will be passed through at cost; Redwood's recoverable amount shall be limited to the lesser of (i) the actual third-party invoice amount plus a 5% administrative fee or (ii) USD 40,000 per calendar quarter." This gives a tighter ceiling (40k) — use if Horizon pushes for broad pass-throughs.

2) True-up language (proposed single sentence to drop into Exhibit D):
"For the purposes of true-up, committed usage tiers will be calculated on an annualized basis (Annualized Commit = Sum of monthly committed units x 12 / number of months in the relevant commitment period). Quarterly true-ups will reconcile actuals against the Annualized Commit; Customer may elect a prospective monthly forecast model subject to Redwood's Forecast SLA and a one-time implementation fee."

I also recommend we preserve a "no retroactive pricing" clause: "Any reduction to Committed Units shall apply prospectively following acceptance of an amended Order Form and shall not retroactively alter prices charged for prior billing periods."

-Karthik

From: Julia Shephard <julia.shephard@horizonhealth.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@horizonhealth.com, legal@horizonhealth.com
Date: Tue, 04 May 2027 14:15:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Order form: packaging, discount safeguards, and pass-through language (redlines)

Marissa — thanks, this is helpful. Legal pushed back on the hard quarterly cap — they prefer a per-instance cap tied to the third-party invoice and an annual aggregate threshold. Their annotated PDF has two asks:

- Replace the flat "USD 50,000 per quarter" with: "per-instance cap equal to the invoice amount + 5% admin fee, with an annual aggregate cap of USD 200,000 unless otherwise agreed in writing."
- Confirm that "packaging seed discounts" are not combinable with promotional onboarding credits (Horizon wants to stack discounts).

Also: if Horizon reduces committed units by 20% in Year 2, what will the pricing look like? Can you provide a simple pro forma showing Year 2 expected spend under (a) pro rata seat discount adjustment, (b) application of a downward true-up, and (c) carry-forward credits limited to 2 quarters?

Attached: Horizon_OrderForm_v3_redline.pdf (legal comments).

Julia

Attachment: Horizon_OrderForm_v3_redline.pdf

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: Julia Shephard <julia.shephard@horizonhealth.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, priya_natarajan@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 05 May 2027 16:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Order form: packaging, discount safeguards, and pass-through language (redlines)

Julia — thanks for the clarity and for sending Legal's annotated PDF. Our counter-proposals below and next steps:

1) Pass-throughs: we can accept the per-instance pass-through (invoice + 5% admin fee) with an annual aggregate cap of USD 175,000 (Redwood cannot accept 200k without C-level approval). If Horizon insists on 200k, I will need to route to Finance for approval.

2) Packaging seed discount stacking: we cannot allow stacking with promotional onboarding credits. Proposed clause: "Promotional credits and seat-based packaging discounts are mutually exclusive and may not be combined for the same billing period."

3) Seat reduction / Year 2 pro forma: attaching a short pro forma with three scenarios (pro rata seat discount, downward true-up, carry-forward limited to 2 quarters). High level: a 20% seat reduction in Year 2 would typically reduce seat-line spend by ~18% after pro rata, but usage true-up could add ~3–6% depending on usage elasticity — see attached spreadsheet.

4) Carry-forward: we can do 2 quarters only; onboarding credits excluded.

5) Fee collar / smoothing: we'll accept smoothing (quarterly aggregation) if Horizon accepts a 3% reconciliation addback on net overages for the smoothing adjustment.

Next steps: I propose a 30-minute call Thursday to walk Legal through the specific redline language so we can agree on a final Order Form for signature. If Horizon accepts the USD 175,000 annual cap and the anti-stacking language, I will circulate an integrated redline and a DocuSign packet.

Calendars: here's a Docusign & meeting link: https://www.docusign.com/embedded?envelopeId=0a1b2c3d

Best,
Marissa Cole
